reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: update through OIMSlotServiceWithChannel → a forwarding link → writeInPlace
reading.floor: the same update through the shipped chain: OIMSlotServiceWithChannel → writeInPlace
reading.caveat: WHAT ONE LINK COSTS, AND THE ROW A TTL LAYER WOULD BE BUILT ON. The added link forwards `mutateSlot` and returns what came back, so the difference between the two numbers is one field load, one arrow-property load and one call — per write. PREDICTED OPERATION COUNT: one extra frame of three machine operations against a write that already does sixteen or more, over 1024 rows per pass. WHICH WAY THE UNMEASURED DIFFERENCE PUSHES: against the deep arm, and only that way. The forwarding link cannot make any part of the write cheaper, so a reading AT OR BELOW 1.00 IS THE INSTRUMENT AND NOT THE DESIGN [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. WHAT IS NOT PRICED HERE: the shape cost. Both arms are isolated, so each runs with ONE shape at the delegating site; a process that mixes link types pays a polymorphic site on top of what this row reads, and no row in this suite measures that yet. THE WRITE AROUND THE LINK IS IDENTICAL ON BOTH ARMS AND IS INSIDE BOTH NUMBERS: `assertNoFrameRunning`, `openChange`/`closeChange` on the channel, the column walk over a ONE-COLUMN patch, the equality call, the store into `slot.entity`, the report to the channel and the frame that closes the pass. ONE OPERATION IS ONE `update` OF ONE COLUMN OF ONE ROW, over a population of 1024, with a frame per pass over the population — so the frame is one part in 1024 of the row. The link is touched ONCE per operation: `update` reaches `mutateSlot` and no other door. A row that removed a column would touch it twice and is not measured here.

reading.ours: update through OIMSlotServiceWithChannel → two forwarding links → writeInPlace
reading.floor: the same update through the shipped chain: OIMSlotServiceWithChannel → writeInPlace
reading.caveat: THE SECOND POINT OF THE CURVE, AND THE ONLY THING THAT SAYS WHETHER A LINK HAS A FLAT PRICE. Read against the row above it: if two links cost twice what one link costs, a chain is a straight line and a consumer can budget by counting links. If the second link costs more than the first, the site has stopped being inlined and the row above under-reads every deeper chain [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. A SINGLE ROW HERE ANSWERS NOTHING; the pair of rows is the measurement. THE WRITE AROUND THE LINK IS IDENTICAL ON BOTH ARMS AND IS INSIDE BOTH NUMBERS: `assertNoFrameRunning`, `openChange`/`closeChange` on the channel, the column walk over a ONE-COLUMN patch, the equality call, the store into `slot.entity`, the report to the channel and the frame that closes the pass. ONE OPERATION IS ONE `update` OF ONE COLUMN OF ONE ROW, over a population of 1024, with a frame per pass over the population — so the frame is one part in 1024 of the row. The link is touched ONCE per operation: `update` reaches `mutateSlot` and no other door. A row that removed a column would touch it twice and is not measured here.

reading.ours: one forwarding stage reached through a stages array, handed its continuation
reading.floor: one forwarding link holding its continuation in a field — the shipped construction
reading.caveat: THE TWO WAYS TO SPELL A CHAIN, WITH EXACTLY ONE STAGE IN EACH so the comparison is about the SPELLING and not about depth. Both arms put one forwarding step between `OIMSlotServiceWithChannel` and `writeInPlace`, and that step does nothing but pass the call on. THE DIFFERENCE, and it is the whole row: the field-bound arm reads `this.inner` and calls a method on it; the parameter arm ALLOCATES THE CONTINUATION — a closure over the stage index and the receiver — and hands it in, on every write. PREDICTED OPERATION COUNT per write: the field arm pays two property loads and a call; the parameter arm pays a closure allocation, an array load, a property load and two calls. WHICH WAY THE UNMEASURED DIFFERENCE PUSHES: against the parameter arm, and only that way — it does everything the field arm does and allocates on top [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. WHAT THE PARAMETER FORM BUYS, which no number here prices: a stage that never names what is under it, so an order can be composed at run time. A reader deciding between the two owes that against whatever this costs. THE WRITE AROUND THE LINK IS IDENTICAL ON BOTH ARMS AND IS INSIDE BOTH NUMBERS: `assertNoFrameRunning`, `openChange`/`closeChange` on the channel, the column walk over a ONE-COLUMN patch, the equality call, the store into `slot.entity`, the report to the channel and the frame that closes the pass. ONE OPERATION IS ONE `update` OF ONE COLUMN OF ONE ROW, over a population of 1024, with a frame per pass over the population — so the frame is one part in 1024 of the row. The link is touched ONCE per operation: `update` reaches `mutateSlot` and no other door. A row that removed a column would touch it twice and is not measured here.

reading.ours: three collections, each with a DIFFERENT forwarding class — the site sees three shapes
reading.floor: three collections with the SAME forwarding class — the site sees one shape
reading.caveat: THE COST NO OTHER ROW IN THIS FILE PRICES, AND THE ONE THAT DECIDES THE SHAPE OF A LAYER API. Every other row here declares `isolate` so each arm runs with ONE shape at `OIMSlotServiceWithChannel`'s `this.inner.mutateSlot`; this row is what those rows deliberately keep out. Both arms write the same number of rows through the same depth over three populations round-robin, and DIFFER ONLY IN HOW MANY CLASSES stand at that one call site: three, or one constructed three times. The three classes have IDENTICAL BODIES — they are written out separately rather than generated, because a factory hands back one class and that is the other arm. WHAT IT DECIDES: whether a consumer may freely mix layer types, or whether a layer API should be one class parameterised by a callback. If this row is flat, the question is answered and nothing follows from it; if it is not, then every count in the rows above is a floor rather than the price [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. WHICH WAY THE UNMEASURED DIFFERENCE PUSHES: against the many-classes arm and only that way — three shapes at a site cannot make it faster than one. WHY THREE AND NOT FIVE: three is inside V8's polymorphic range, so the row reads what a POLYMORPHIC site costs against a monomorphic one. What a MEGAMORPHIC site costs is a different row and this suite does not have it. THE WRITE AROUND THE LINK IS IDENTICAL ON BOTH ARMS AND IS INSIDE BOTH NUMBERS: `assertNoFrameRunning`, `openChange`/`closeChange` on the channel, the column walk over a ONE-COLUMN patch, the equality call, the store into `slot.entity`, the report to the channel and the frame that closes the pass. ONE OPERATION IS ONE `update` OF ONE COLUMN OF ONE ROW, over a population of 1024, with a frame per pass over the population — so the frame is one part in 1024 of the row. The link is touched ONCE per operation: `update` reaches `mutateSlot` and no other door. A row that removed a column would touch it twice and is not measured here.
